title: Δημάδης ὁ ῥήτωρ
source: Émile Chambry, Ésope: Fables, texte établi et traduit (Les Belles Lettres, Paris, 1927), fable 96 (= Perry 63). Text as printed, including Chambry's editorial punctuation (« »). Pronunciation: reconstructed Attic, after W. S. Allen, Vox Graeca. Romanization: standard classical transliteration (ē/ō; th/ph/ch; y for υ, u in diphthongs; h = rough breathing; ēi/āi/ōi for iota subscript; accents omitted).

sentences.t: Δημάδης ὁ ῥήτωρ δημηγορῶν ποτε ἐν Ἀθήναις, ἐκείνων μὴ πάνυ τι αὐτῷ προσεχόντων, ἐδεήθη αὐτῶν ὅπως ἐπιτρέψωσιν αὐτῷ Αἰσώπειον μῦθον εἰπεῖν.
sentences.tr: Dēmadēs ho rhētōr dēmēgorōn pote en Athēnais, ekeinōn mē pany ti autōi prosechontōn, edeēthē autōn hopōs epitrepsōsin autōi Aisōpeion mython eipein.
sentences.l: Demades the orator, once speaking before the people at Athens — they not attending to him very much — asked them that they should permit him to tell an Aesopic fable.
sentences.i: Demades the orator was once addressing the people at Athens, and since they were paying him no great attention, he begged them to let him tell a fable of Aesop's.
sentences.n: Demades was an Athenian orator of the fourth century, famous for the quickness of his tongue. ἐκείνων … προσεχόντων is a genitive absolute whose subject has not yet been named: 'they' are the assembly, implied in δημηγορῶν, speaking before the δῆμος. προσέχω (with τὸν νοῦν understood) takes a dative, 'to attend to'. δέομαι, 'I ask', takes a genitive of the person asked.

sentences.t: Τῶν δὲ συγχωρησάντων αὐτῷ, ἀρξάμενος ἔλεγε· « Δήμητρα καὶ χελιδὼν καὶ ἔγχελυς τὴν αὐτὴν ὁδὸν ἐβάδιζον· γενομένων δὲ αὐτῶν κατά τινα ποταμόν, ἡ μὲν χελιδὼν ἔπτη, ἡ δὲ ἔγχελυς κατέδυ· » καὶ ταῦτα εἰπὼν ἐσιώπησεν.
sentences.tr: Tōn de synchōrēsantōn autōi, arxamenos elege· « Dēmētra kai chelidōn kai enchelys tēn autēn hodon ebadizon· genomenōn de autōn kata tina potamon, hē men chelidōn eptē, hē de enchelys katedy· » kai tauta eipōn esiōpēsen.
sentences.l: And they having granted it to him, having begun he was saying: « Demeter and a swallow and an eel were walking the same road; and when they came to be at a certain river, the swallow flew up, and the eel dived down; » and having said this he fell silent.
sentences.i: They granted it, and he began: « Demeter and a swallow and an eel were travelling the same road; and when they came to a river, the swallow flew up and the eel went under; » and having said that, he stopped.
sentences.n: Chambry prints Δήμητρα where classical Attic has the nominative Δημήτηρ; the later language forms a first-declension nominative Δημήτρα, and the article ἡ standing before it in the next sentence shows it is nominative here. ἔπτη is the aorist of πέτομαι, κατέδυ of καταδύομαι: each creature takes the road proper to its own nature, and the goddess is left standing at the bank. The story stops exactly where the audience most wants it to go on.

sentences.t: Ἐρομένων δὲ αὐτῶν· « Ἡ οὖν Δήμητρα τί ἔπαθεν ; » ἔφη· « Κεχόλωται ὑμῖν, οἵτινες τὰ τῆς πόλεως πράγματα ἐάσαντες Αἰσωπείων μύθων ἀντέχεσθε. »
sentences.tr: Eromenōn de autōn· « Hē oun Dēmētra ti epathen ; » ephē· « Kecholōtai hymin, hoitines ta tēs poleōs pragmata easantes Aisōpeiōn mythōn antechesthe. »
sentences.l: And they having asked: « What then did Demeter suffer? » he said: « She is enraged at you, who, having let go the affairs of the city, cling to Aesopic fables. »
sentences.i: And when they asked: « And what became of Demeter? » he said: « She is enraged at you, who let the city's business go and hang on fables of Aesop. »
sentences.n: τί ἔπαθεν is literally 'what did she suffer?' — the ordinary Greek way of asking what became of someone. κεχόλωται is a perfect with present force, 'she is in a rage', and takes a dative of the person she is angry with. ἀντέχομαι in the middle takes a genitive of what one holds on to. οἵτινες is the general relative, 'you, being the sort who…' — the reproach is aimed at their character, not at one lapse.

sentences.t: Οὕτω καὶ τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἀλόγιστοί εἰσιν ὅσοι τῶν μὲν ἀναγκαίων ὀλιγωροῦσι, τὰ δὲ πρὸς ἡδονὴν μᾶλλον αἱροῦνται.
sentences.tr: Houtō kai tōn anthrōpōn alogistoi eisin hosoi tōn men anankaiōn oligōrousi, ta de pros hēdonēn mallon hairountai.
sentences.l: So too, among men, those are without judgement who make light of what is necessary and choose rather the things that tend to pleasure.
sentences.n: ὀλιγωρέω, 'to think little of', takes a genitive. μέν … δέ sets the necessary against the pleasant. τὰ πρὸς ἡδονήν is 'the things that make for pleasure'. ἀλόγιστος is 'without λογισμός', without reckoning.
